caption:
🚆 Britain vs Germany — every train of the same day, Thursday 15 October 2026.

Same rules on both sides: long-distance and regional trains, with the Elizabeth line, London Overground and Merseyrail left out on one side, the S-Bahn on the other. Germany ran over 26,000 trains that day against Britain's 19,000, yet minute by minute the two stay close: about 1,800 trains moving at Germany's morning peak, 1,540 at Britain's, and around 1,300 on each side at noon. Britain fits that traffic into less than 60% of Germany's area. London's commuter operators (Southern, Thameslink, South Western) are counted as mainline railways, which flatters the British side a little.

📊 Data: National Rail GTFS by travelwhiz (CC BY 4.0) · DB/DELFI GTFS by gtfs.de (CC BY 4.0). Trains follow the real tracks (operators' shapes, © OpenStreetMap); positions interpolated between stops.
🌍 Relief: AWS Terrain Tiles · Natural Earth.
